faq.a: Kairat is associated with the Arabic form خَيْرَت, whose core sense is kairat; goodness, blessing.

faq.q: What is the origin of Kairat?
faq.a: Kairat is associated with Arabic. Kairat is Arabic خَيْرَة (Khayra), meaning 'goodness, blessing'. It is widely used as a male given name in Central Asia.
Yes — the underlying form خَيْرَت is Arabic.
Kairat can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Kairat should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Khayrat is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Kairat mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Kairat is rendered خیرت and carries the sense خیرت، بھلائی.

faq.q: What does Kairat mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Kairat is rendered خیرت and carries the sense خیرت، نیکی.
A romanized syllable approximation is kai-rat. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Kairat?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Kairat, kairat. Script forms are خيرت, خَيْرَت, خیرت, ख़ैरत.

faq.q: Is Kairat a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
